name: Barbell Anderson Squat / Bottom-Up Squat
description: The Anderson squat begins at the bottom of the squat position with the bar resting on safety pins inside a power rack. Because there is no eccentric loading or stretch reflex, the lifter must generate force from a dead stop, making it an excellent tool for building strength in the most difficult portion of the squat. It is named after the legendary powerlifter Paul Anderson.

execution.starting_position: Set the safety pins inside the power rack at your bottom squat position (hip crease at or below knee level). Crouch under the bar and position it on your upper traps or rear delts, feet in your normal squat stance.
execution.setup_instructions: Set pins at the depth you want to work from. Load a conservative weight initially. Duck under the bar in the bottom position.
steps: Step 1: Position yourself under the bar at the bottom, brace the core hard, and take a deep breath.
Step 2: Drive through the entire foot explosively from a dead stop, pushing the knees outward.
Step 3: Extend the hips and knees together, rising to full lockout.
Step 4: Lower yourself slowly back to the pins. Rest 1-2 seconds between each rep to eliminate the stretch reflex.
execution.breathing_instructions: Brace fully before each individual rep. Exhale at the top.
common_mistakes: Using the bounce off the pins instead of a true dead stop
Pins set too high, reducing the training stimulus
safety_considerations: The power rack safeties must be set at a height that allows full depth
Start with significantly less weight than your regular squat maximum
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Concentric only — no eccentric loading. Set pins at or below parallel.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Explosive concentric from dead stop. Slow controlled return to pins.
coaching_cues: Eliminate any bounce off the pins
